attack_mechanism: The assignment `lsu_priv <= mstatus_mpp when mstatus_mprv = '1' else prv_level` makes `mstatus_mprv` the privilege-source selector. `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.cpu_trap` reaches that selector or one of its CSR update controls; the intervening RTL assignments are qualified by `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.cpu_trap`, `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mprv`. A transient or persistent fault on `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.cpu_trap` during CSR update or request issue can flip the effective privilege used for that load/store. The supporting RTL chain is `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.cpu_trap -> neorv32_cpu_control.trap_env -> neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl_o.lsu_priv`. The LSU selects the wrong privilege source and applies an unintended protection domain to the pending memory request.

For a load or store issued while `mstatus_mprv = 1`, the control unit assigns `ctrl_o.lsu_priv <= csr.mstatus_mpp`. `neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl_nxt.csr_we` can alter the CSR write, trap/debug return, or stored `mstatus_mpp` value used by that MPRV branch; the intervening RTL assignments are qualified by `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.csr_we`, `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mprv`. A transient or persistent fault on `neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl_nxt.csr_we` during CSR update or request issue can flip the effective privilege used for that load/store. The supporting RTL chain is `neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl_nxt.csr_we -> neorv32_cpu.ctrl.csr_we -> neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mpp -> neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl_o.lsu_priv`. The LSU request metadata carries an unintended effective privilege, allowing a memory access to be checked as a more privileged operation.
